### 2. Your role

Traffic engineer for the applicant. You advise the design team on access, parking and circulation while the design develops, and prepare the traffic report the consent authority needs. Plans come from the architect in DWG and PDF.

### 3. Scope by stage

Price each stage that applies as a lump sum; surveys are priced per location.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off | Pricing |
|---|---|---|
| Parking and access advice | Site inspection; review of plans and controls; advice on access, heavy vehicle circulation, loading and parking layout | Lump sum |
| Traffic and parking report | Traffic generation and distribution; network impact (using the modelling stage where it applies); parking provision against the DCP and demand; access and AS 2890 compliance; swept paths for the design vehicle; pedestrian, cyclist and end-of-trip review; safety. 1 draft, 1 final | Lump sum |
| Assessment response | Up to 1 response(s) to council or TfNSW requests; 1 meeting(s) | Lump sum |
| Conditions review | Review of the traffic conditions in the consent; reply letter if needed | Lump sum |
| Construction traffic management plan | Construction traffic management plan for council approval, or review of the contractor's plan (say which in R2); traffic control plans | Lump sum |

Price these separately; they are not in the base fee.

| Option | Deliverable | Why it is optional |
|---|---|---|
| Review of the developed design | Ramps, parking and loading checked against the consent conditions as the design develops or the contractor changes it; signage and line-marking submissions to the local traffic committee | Client opts in |
| Car park certification | Design certification of the car park, access and loading against AS 2890 for the construction certificate; completed car park certification after construction | Client opts in |
| Green travel plan | Travel plan meeting the condition or DCP requirement | Price as an option: needed only if a consent condition or the DCP requires a travel plan. |

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan revisions assessed | 1 | Report drafts | 1 draft, 1 final |

### 5. Scope position

I = included in the fee · O = optional, price as a separate line · X = excluded (the party named does it).
Service levels in this table are set for a complex project (Use generates heavy vehicle movements). Technical items follow the project's own facts.
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Vehicle schedule (waste, emergency, service and operator vehicles); ramps, gradients, headroom, sight lines and pedestrian conflicts checked against the current architect and civil layouts | I |
| Consultation with council traffic engineers and TfNSW while preparing the report | I |
| Bicycle parking and end-of-trip assessment | I |
| Parking demand reduction measures | I |
| Alternative schemes tested | O |
| Swept paths for every loading dock and design vehicle | I |
| Microsimulation beyond SIDRA | X: not required |
| Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design team; state its stage and scope in R2 | O. Price as an option: an audit is needed only for works in a public road. |
| Design of works in the public road (signals, intersections) | X: civil engineer (separate engagement) (to be appointed) |
| Expert witness, Land and Environment Court | X: client (separate engagement) |

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached). Your own terms and conditions do not apply; list any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises a change in scope, work beyond an allowance or a change in fee, under the agreement. Work beyond an allowance without that instruction is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, and the signed-off design is the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a change the client asks for after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors or omissions, and coordinating your work with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days. Payment does not depend on an authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Send questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23. Answers are issued to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- No commencement payment; the final report is not held back pending payment.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.

R2 Deliverables list: For each deliverable: format, stage, review rounds, who prepares it and who receives it. Say whether editable source files are included and what reliance others may place on them. Report, model files, swept path drawings and letters.
R3 Hourly rates: Rates excl. GST, used only for work authorised in writing beyond the allowances. Roles: Director · Senior engineer · Traffic engineer · Graduate · CAD or graphics. Per-meeting rates if you use them.
R4 Team: Named lead and their availability by stage, with % time; subconsultants and their roles. Resources must match the program in R7. Credentials: CPEng or RPEQ, road safety auditor level, traffic control planner.
R5 Experience: Two or three comparable projects in the last five years, each with a referee. Traffic reports for this use, in the same LGA or state road context.
R6 Departures: Each departure from sections 3 to 6 and from the agreement: the clause or item, the change you propose and its effect on fee and time; or write "nil". Departures are evaluated. A general exclusion or qualification not listed here is treated as non-compliant.
R7 Program: Weeks by stage against the durations given, separating your working time, authority assessment time and the dates you need inputs from others.
R8 Insurance and compliance: Professional indemnity $5 million and public liability $20 million, with insurer and expiry; workers compensation; a quality, safety and environmental management system (certified to ISO 9001, 45001 and 14001, or an equivalent system you describe); conflicts of interest. Conflict of interest statement.
R9 Reimbursables: "Included in the fee" (preferred), or each item with its rate. Included is preferred.

### Before issue — resolve or accept

**Rules await owner review**: The traffic and parking services rules are a draft. Drafting and editing work; issue stays blocked until the owner marks them reviewed.

**Blocks issue — Gross floor area: sources disagree (2135 vs 2895)**: Set the one figure every firm prices from.

**Green travel plan required by a condition or the DCP: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Green travel plan.

**Works in a public road or intersection: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design team; state its stage and scope in R2.
